title: Harmanpreet Lost the Series. She Is Not Worried About the World Cup.
excerpt: India's women fell 2-1 to England in Taunton. Four days later, the T20 World Cup begins. The captain says the positives outweigh the defeat.
body:
Harmanpreet Kaur lost the series decider in Taunton. Within 24 hours, she was already reframing the defeat as preparation.

India's women lost the three-match T20I series against England 2-1 on June 2, falling in the deciding match at the Cooper Associates County Ground. For most captains, losing a bilateral series days before a World Cup would prompt panic. Harmanpreet, who has led India through enough near-misses to fill a highlight reel of heartbreak, responded differently.

"We have seen lot of positives going forward to WC," Harmanpreet said after the Taunton loss, her voice carrying the measured confidence of someone who has been in this position before. "Despite the series loss, I think there are things we can take forward."

## The Context That Changes Everything

India are not just any team walking into the ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026, which begins on June 12 in England. They are the reigning ICC Women's Cricket World Cup champions, having beaten South Africa in the 50-over final last year. That triumph transformed women's cricket in India — participation rates surged, the WPL attracted record investment, and Harmanpreet's squad became household names in a country where the men's game had monopolized attention for decades.

"We have seen that during last year's World Cup when we won," Harmanpreet said at the captains' press conference ahead of the T20 tournament. "After that, we have seen massive change. Many girls, they're coming to play cricket, and I think when we do well a lot of things change."

The T20 World Cup is the one trophy that has eluded this generation of Indian women. They reached the final in 2020, where Australia dismantled them at the Melbourne Cricket Ground. They exited in the group stage in the 2024 edition. This time, they arrive in England as the world's dominant 50-over side, trying to translate that supremacy into the shortest format.

## The England Series as Rehearsal

The T20I series against England was always designed as a dress rehearsal. India won the opener at Chelmsford convincingly, with Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma setting the tone at the top. The hosts fought back to level the series in Bristol, then clinched the decider in Taunton.

But Harmanpreet's assessment was not spin. India used all 16 squad members across the three matches, rotating through combinations that would be impractical in a World Cup but invaluable for understanding which partnerships work in English conditions. Jemimah Rodrigues batted at three, four, and five across consecutive matches and declared herself happy to slot in wherever the team needed.

The series also exposed what needs fixing. India's death bowling leaked runs in the final two matches, and the middle order wobbled when Mandhana fell cheaply. With the T20 World Cup group stage beginning in four days, those are problems that need solving, not ignoring.

## South Africa Again

India's group includes South Africa, the team they beat in the 50-over World Cup final and the side that has finished runner-up in the last two T20 World Cup editions. Captain Laura Wolvaardt has recalled Shabnim Ismail and Dane van Niekerk, two experienced campaigners who know English conditions well.

"I think someone like Shabs, since she retired, we've sort of been lacking that really fast baller in our lineup," Wolvaardt said. "Same with Dane. She offers so much from a leadership point of view."

A rematch between India and South Africa in the group stage would be one of the early blockbusters of the tournament. Both sides believe they are the best team in women's cricket. On June 12, they begin trying to prove it.

## What NRI Fans Should Know

The ICC Women's T20 World Cup 2026 runs from June 12 to July 2 in England. For NRI viewers in the United States, matches will start in the early morning hours (IST afternoon), making them accessible on weekends and manageable on weekday mornings for East Coast viewers.

India's group matches will be played across multiple English venues. The knockout stages, if India progress, will likely overlap with the FIFA World Cup in North America and the India A tri-series in Sri Lanka — a rare convergence that gives Indian sports fans three simultaneous tournaments to track.

Harmanpreet, who turns 37 during the tournament, knows this may be her last T20 World Cup as captain. Her legacy in the 50-over format is secure. The T20 crown is the missing piece.
